registered_at: 2026-11-02, before any model call of this experiment
question: When gemini-3.8-flash omits a hidden (net-invisible) sigma event in its executable mechanism, does it know the corresponding hidden intermediate when asked in free text?
model: gemini-3.8-flash via http://LLM-GATEWAY-1.example:8080/v1, reasoning_effort=high, temperature=0.2, max_tokens=65536, one sample per condition
cases: J3 set: FukuyamaBench held-out primary T0-T2 (123) + dev (24) = 147; 95 have hidden events; 174 probeable events (90 heavy-atom, 84 H-transfer); 12 events without a distinct hidden species are excluded

conditions.E: executable PGL mechanism, same prompt and audit turn as J3 (agent_v2.generate)
conditions.S: free-text mechanism with SMILES of each intermediate in <intermediates>
conditions.G: S plus a generic, case-independent cue to consider short-lived species not visible in the overall equation

scoring: E uses an event if the predicted path forms and breaks the same H-anonymised pair. S/G recall an event if any listed SMILES matches a GT hidden species in the event window by sigma-graph key (heavy-atom connectivity + H count per heavy atom; bond orders and charges ignored). Skeleton key (no H) is a sensitivity analysis.
primary: Heavy-atom hidden events omitted in E: fraction recalled in S or G (exact sigma-key), case-clustered bootstrap 95% CI.
secondary: same quantity for all events and for H-transfer events
recall in E vs S vs G
G - S paired difference (does a generic cue activate knowledge)
E sigma-L1 on all 147 cases (comparison with the main law)
limitations_declared_in_advance: one model, one sample per condition
free-text recall is a recall test, not a recognition test
S/G and E differ in format as well as in cueing
